do.name: Grand Place and Place des Heros
do.detail: Two linked squares in Arras next door, 155 arcaded gable fronts in brick and sandstone, Hispano Flemish and nine centuries old as a market place. Almost all of it was rebuilt after 1918, carefully enough that you cannot tell.

do.name: Wellington Quarry
do.detail: Chalk workings that New Zealand tunnellers joined up in 1916 and 1917 so that 24,000 men could wait 20 m under the German line before the assault of 9 April 1917. Ninety minutes with a guide, and it stays at 11 degrees down there whatever the weather.

do.name: Climb the belfry
do.detail: The town hall's belfry, listed by UNESCO in 2005 with the other belfries of Belgium and France, and voted France's favourite monument in 2015. A lift and then stairs reach the viewing platform.

do.name: Canadian National Vimy Memorial
do.detail: Fifteen minutes north: preserved trenches and tunnels under two white pylons, for the Canadians who took the ridge in 1917.

do.name: The boves under the squares
do.detail: Twenty kilometres of galleries cut into the chalk from the 10th century on, first as quarries, then cellars, then shelters in both wars. Guided from the town hall.
